files_what: the files this run made. Read a file only when it is listed here: one named under left_out or failed was not made by this run, and a copy of it in the folder is an older one.
written_without_what: files made without an input that only adds detail, and what each then lacks

temperature.source: NASA POWER, POWER Climatology API v2.10.1, regional endpoint; data source named by the service for each parameter: T2M: MERRA2; T2M_MAX: MERRA2, POWER; T2M_MIN: MERRA2, POWER; TS: MERRA2 (MERRA-2 is NASA's reanalysis)
temperature.what_it_is: Air temperature 2 m above the ground (mean, and the highest and lowest hour of the period) and surface temperature (mean), in degrees Celsius, for each calendar month over the years of the period, at the MERRA-2 grid point nearest to the cell centre, as served by the NASA POWER climatology service. Model values (a reanalysis), not measurements at the cell. Many cells share one grid point.
temperature.what_it_is_not: Not a measurement at the cell and not the temperature during the hours of low Sun: it is a mean over all hours of the month and over a grid box about 55 km tall and 15 to 35 km wide at these latitudes, at the mean height of that box (grid_elev_m), which near an ice sheet or a mountain coast can lie hundreds of metres above the cell. t2m_max_c and t2m_min_c are the extremes of all the years covered, not a typical day's high and low. It enters no score.

fields.t2m_c: T2M: mean air temperature 2 m above the ground, all hours of day and night, by calendar month
fields.ts_c: TS: mean temperature of the surface itself (skin temperature), all hours, by calendar month

temperature.by_bin_rule: temperature.by_bin(row) gives 36 ten-day values, each bin taking the month of its middle day (bin // 3); bin = min((day_of_year - 1) // 10, 35)

lunar_comparison.lunar_what: LRO Diviner annual mean temperature 2 cm under the surface (model-based): lowest and highest of the area means of the lunar sites, and the coldest triangle of any site
lunar_comparison.sentence: Earth does not match the Moon in temperature: in their best ten-day periods the Earth places above have mean air temperatures between -11 and 10 C, while the lunar south-pole sites are at annual mean temperatures 2 cm under the surface of -185 to -130 C averaged over each site, down to -244 C in the coldest spot (LRO Diviner Polar Resource Product: model values, not measurements); a field test there rehearses the light, not the cold.

temperature.named_places_what: ten_day_mean_of_daily_series: mean air temperature (t2m_c), mean daily maximum and minimum (t2m_daily_max_c, t2m_daily_min_c) and surface temperature (ts_c) of the ten-day period, from the daily series of the same grid point; degrees C
temperature.grid_height_what: mean height in metres of the model's grid box for each area, in the page's area order; null where the service named none. A box far above the area reads too cold.
